transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date/Time: 2026-12-10 16:00 UTC
- Duration: 72 minutes (approx)
- Platform: Zoom (recording on)
- Attendees: Maya, Liam (Redwood); Aisha, Carlos, Priya, Samir (Helix)

Summary:
Quick kickoff for a sprint-style evaluation of quantization profiles (INT8 vs FP8) and the latency/fidelity tradeoffs using Redwood Optimize sandbox. Goal is to determine default qprofile for Helix prod pilot and validate risk/rollback plan for canary rollouts.

Topics covered:
- current inference stack and constraints (on-prem vs cloud)
- dataset/prompt characteristics (medical triage + long context notes)
- INT8 vs FP8 expected speedups and quality risks
- rollout and fallback strategies (canary, model fallback, prefix caching)
- security/compliance considerations (KMS, SOC2, VPC)

Transcript body (timestamps are approximate, auto-transcribed with occasional errors):
[00:00] Maya (AE): hey everyone thanks for making time this afternoon, quick icebreaker — is the goal still to get a pilot live by end of January?
[00:06] Priya (Head of AI): yes, end of Jan would be ideal. We need to be confident there's no regression on the clinical triage prompts, those are our must-not-break set.
[00:12] Aisha: yeah and to add, lots of the inputs are long, like 1k to 3k token notes, so latency tail is a real user pain.
[00:18] Liam (SE): thanks, that’s super helpful. Today we'll run through how Redwood Optimize suggests qprofiles, what INT8 vs FP8 looked like in similar med workloads, and propose a sprint plan. I will share the sandbox benchmark sheet in chat now — link: (shared qprofile-bench.xlsx).
[00:32] Carlos (Platform): quick infra note, currently we run models on our private cluster with a Triton layer and internal KV cache. We also have a VPC connection for cloud bursts.
[00:38] Maya: great, that's common. two quick clarifying Qs — what throughput do you need? and what's your SLO for p95/p99 latency?
[00:44] Aisha: baseline is about 120 qps peak across user-facing endpoints, with p95 target under 600 ms. p99 we tolerate up to 1.2s for long docs but prefer lower.
[00:54] Liam: got it — that p95 target is reachable with batching and INT8 in a lot of cases, but FP8 can give a further speedup at some quality cost depending on model architecture and prompt distribution.
[01:03] Priya: can you quantify 'some' cost? clinicians will push back on hallucinations.
[01:08] Liam: yep so from our runs on similar Llama-derived family models — INT8 usually gives 1.6–2.2x throughput vs FP16 baseline and FP8 tends to be 2.3–3x depending on kernel efficiency. Quality-wise, INT8 often holds parity on classification-like tasks; FP8 can introduce subtle token-level shifts—more apparent on open-ended narrative completions.
[01:28] Aisha: okay so for our triage classifier INT8 probably safe, but for the discharge summaries FP8 might be risky.
[01:35] Maya: that's exactly the tradeoff we want to test in the sprint. we can pick a conservative qprofile for triage endpoints and a more cautious rollout for summarization.
[01:42] Samir (Security): question on encryption — if we run Redwood Optimize in our VPC or dedicated, how do you handle KMS keys? We need HSM-backed key support and audit logs.
[01:49] Liam: yes, for Private/dedicated we integrate with customer KMS/HSM; logs are shipped to your cloud logging endpoint and we can also enable extended audit retention. we'll send the SOC2 + KMS integration doc after the call.
[02:01] Carlos: perfect. also curious about automatic fallback — if FP8 regression is detected, can we auto-fallback to INT8 or FP16 for affected prompts?
[02:08] Liam: yes, Redwood runtime supports routing policies: detect quality drop via heuristics or eval webhook and route to fallback model variant. we typically suggest canary rollout with a 1% traffic needle then ramp, and keep KV/prefix caches warmed for both variants to avoid cold miss latency spikes.
[02:22] Maya: I'll show the Optimize console now — small screen share hiccup — ok, can you all see the qprofile explorer?
[02:29] Priya: yes seeing it. the UI looks similar to what we saw in the quickstart.
[02:33] Liam: on the left you can pick model family, on the right we surface suggested qprofiles: conservative INT8, balanced INT8+FP8 hybrid, aggressive FP8. we also show per-prompt diff snapshots next to sample metrics: ROUGE, token entropy, hallucination score (approx), and latency p95.
[02:50] Aisha: how do you compute hallucination score? that metric worries me — it's usually heuristics.
[02:55] Liam: good call, it's heuristics combined with reference-based checks for the evaluation subset you provide. we flag divergences from gold references, contradictions, and confidence tokens. it's not a replacement for human review but it helps prioritize regressions.
[03:08] Maya: note that the heuristic thresholds are adjustable per-customer. for clinical we'll want tighter limits.
[03:12] Aisha: yep.
[03:15] [03:15] — transcript picks up with a sample benchmark run exported — Liam: I'm loading a quick run we completed on a similar customer, call out the important columns: delta-quality, relative-cost-per-token, p95-latency-ms.
[03:30] Liam: here’s an example: INT8 gave median +1% ROUGE, p95 down from 480ms to 310ms, cost per token -42%. FP8 gave ROUGE -3% (on open summaries), p95 of 260ms, cost -60%.
[03:47] Priya: that -3% ROUGE on FP8 is non-trivial for clinical text. how noisy are those numbers?
[03:52] Liam: the noise depends on the eval set. For our runs we used a 2k prompt eval set. we'll obviously run this on your 100 canonical prompts to get a Helix-specific signal.
[04:02] Carlos: what's the failure mode we should watch for — is it hallucination, token drift, or response truncation?
[04:06] Liam: all three. FP8 can produce token drift over long context due to subtle distributional shifts. That's where rollback policies and prompt-level routing help. Also watch for quantization-sensitive ops in the model like specialized attention — our kernel selector flags layers that are risky to quantize and we can keep them in FP16 while quantizing others.
[04:25] Aisha: can we do hybrid profiles where critical layers stay FP16?
[04:28] Liam: absolutely — the qprofile supports per-layer and per-block precision. we call them hybrid qprofiles; they often get the best of both worlds.
[04:34] [05:00] Maya: we're proposing a two-track sprint: 1) quick INT8 baseline across triage endpoints, 2) hybrid/FP8 experiments for summarization with stricter evaluation and slow ramp. we'll run nightbench jobs and produce a prioritized regression list.
[05:15] Priya: sounds good. timeline?
[05:18] Maya: goal: run first sweep by 12/15, review on 12/22, pilot rollout planning 12/27–01/05.
[05:25] Samir: from security side, we need a threat model for the fallback path and audit of the routing logs. is that something Redwood provides?
[05:31] Liam: yes we can provide routing audit exports and a recommended threat model doc. also for private deployments the routing decision points can be inside your VPC console, so logs never leave your environment.
[05:42] Carlos: one infra gotcha — our KV cache is tied to Triton. if we switch models or variants frequently we may lose cache and see latency spikes. any mitigations?
[05:49] Liam: yep, keep compatible KV cache formats or use prefix-based warming during canary. we also support on-the-fly KV migration for compatible models. I'll add notes for your Triton config in the runbook.
[05:59] Aisha: what's required from our side for the first benchmark?
[06:03] Maya: we'll need the canonical prompt set (100), 200 session traces to match real traffic, and access details for the sandbox if you want Dedicated mode. otherwise we can run in Redwood-hosted sandbox with obfuscated data.
[06:14] Aisha: we'll upload prompts and data by the 17th.
[06:17] [06:17] — interruption/overlap — Speaker 6: I have a billing Q, but happy to sync offline.
[06:22] Maya: sure we'll handle billing offline. quick question — any non-negotiable regulatory constraints besides SOC2?
[06:28] Samir: data residency — some patient records must remain in-region. and we need HSM keys for any PHI processing.
[06:34] Liam: we support region pinning and HSM-backed KMS. for on-prem or air-gapped we also have an appliance option.
[06:41] Priya: what about model rollbacks — who is responsible for the rollback decision if a regression is detected in production?
[06:46] Maya: typically we propose an ops runbook: Redwood suggests automated heuristics and holds an AE/SE runway for advisory rollback. final rollback decision is customer-controlled, but we can provide automation for immediate fallback traffic routing.
[06:58] Carlos: ok that level of control is good.
[07:02] [07:02] — Liam shares a sample canary config — Liam: here's a 3-phase canary: 1% -> 10% -> 50% ramp with continuous eval gating. auto-fallback to INT8 if eval delta > threshold or human pause.
[07:19] Aisha: what metrics are in that gate?
[07:22] Liam: we recommend token-level alignment, ROUGE/F1 for extraction, latency p95, and hallucination heuristic. thresholds are configurable.
[07:31] Maya: quick check — is there appetite to try FP8 at 1% traffic for summarization first, or only after hybrid per-layer profiles?
[07:37] Priya: let's start hybrid per-layer; if that looks clean we'll trial FP8 at 1% with strict monitoring.
[07:44] Maya: noted.
[07:48] [07:48] — closing minutes recap — Maya: recap of action items: Redwood runs initial INT8 sweep and hybrid experiments in sandbox, Helix uploads prompts/traces, Redwood sends SOC2 and KMS doc, schedule follow-up 12/22. Any blockers?
[07:59] Priya: none from product.
[08:01] Carlos: none.
[08:03] Samir: send security docs please.
[08:05] Maya: will do. thanks everyone, we'll follow up with calendar invites.
